title: Shadow tokens do not switch in a locally dark subtree
description: Introduced by the ecl.2 shadow refactor and caught in Storybook's side-by-side light/dark token panels. The refactor made the shadow layer colours semantic (base/_dark) and gave each elevation one primitive that referenced them. But shadow primitives are declared on :root, and a custom property that references another resolves in the scope where it is DEFINED, not where it is used, so the :root-level var stayed on the light colour inside a [data-color-mode=dark] subtree. dropShadow was unaffected because its var is declared on the element that uses it.
close_reason: The light/dark switch moved back onto the shadow semantic token, which Panda re-declares under :where(.dark, [data-color-mode=dark]) and therefore resolves in the scoped subtree. Each elevation has a light and a dark primitive again, but both are still generated from ONE geometry definition, so the point of the refactor is kept. dropShadow keeps reading the semantic colour, which is correct because its var is declared on the using element. Verified in a browser against the generated CSS: inside a [data-color-mode=dark] subtree, raised resolves to rgba(1,4,4,0.5) and overflow keeps its wider 0.75rem dark blur, while the light panel resolves to rgba(30,31,33,0.25) and 0.5rem.

title: Dismissable Chip renders the dismiss button outside the pill
description: The container was a bare inline-flex wrapper with gap 1 and no background, while body painted the pill. Because the dismiss button is a sibling of body rather than a child (a button cannot nest in body's button), the X fell outside the painted pill and read as belonging to the next chip as much as its own. The dismissable variant in the recipe was an empty stub, { body: {} }, and git log shows container never had a background in any commit. Reported by Shaun from Storybook 2026-09-06.
close_reason: Adopted the Cetec DS structure at Shaun's direction. The container is now always rendered, is the root, and paints the pill; body is transparent and keeps typography, padding, focus ring and interactivity. Verified in Storybook: dismiss button sits inside the pill flush against body across sizes and slot combinations, and selected, disabled, loading and deleted all resolve on the container. Deliberate deviation from the DS: the dismiss button no longer paints a hover background, because bg.neutral tokens are semi-transparent (#1717170F over #17171724 composites to about 26 percent, not the 14 percent the token specifies). The icon fill carries the affordance instead. Also fixed borderRadius 'full' on dismissButton, which is not a radii token here and resolved to 0.

title: Remove compoundVariants from button, chip, textInput, listItem, badge, card recipes so variant props are responsive (DS parity)
description: Panda types a recipe's variant props as plain literals (not ConditionalValue) when the recipe declares compoundVariants. Cetec-Design-System has zero compoundVariants in these six recipes; okshaun's June port kept them (size x iconBefore/iconAfter padding). Result: responsive sizes from FieldContext/SlotContext cannot reach these recipes, and Button.tsx / Chip.tsx carry casts marked with this issue id. Fold the size x icon padding into the size variants (selector or CSS-variable based, as the DS recipes do), delete the compoundVariants, regenerate, remove the casts, and add the responsive staticCss coverage already declared in panda.config.ts recipeOverrides.
close_reason: Resolved by adopting the Cetec recipes for card, listItem, chip, badge, textInput and button rather than only stripping compoundVariants, at Shaun's direction: those components are production-hardened and okshaun's own semantic tokens carry the styling. Also ported the two shared foundations the Cetec recipes depend on - globalBaseStyles and listDensity - and moved list and listItemGroup onto the same density abstraction. Every variant prop on all six recipes is now ConditionalValue. Two Cetec-only tokens failed silently and were handled: cta's gold palette (variant dropped, no okshaun equivalent) and text.selected.hovered (mapped to text.selected). tag still declares compoundVariants, and so does Cetec's tag, so it is left alone. Verified in Storybook: list and menu density unchanged at compact 10/3 and comfortable 12/7, textInput sizes 24/32/40/48, all eight button variants render.

title: filter utility is registered under a non-CSS property name and has no values
description: preset.ts registered the utility as 'filtersProperty', which is not a CSS property, so Panda generated an inert style prop typed as free-form string | number and emitted no CSS for it. The utility also declared values: 'filters', a token category that does not exist, and the token-shaped 'filters' map in filters.ts was never registered in the theme. Net effect: the library's named invert, blur and none filters were unreachable and 'filter' offered only Panda's base 'auto'. Found while porting ecl.2.
close_reason: Registered as 'filter' rather than 'filtersProperty', extending Panda's base filter utility. filters.ts now exports a plain filterValues map (auto, invert, blur, none) consumed directly by the utility instead of pointing at a nonexistent token category, and filterAutoValue stays the single source for the composable slot string that dropShadow also writes through. Generated types now read filter: 'auto' | 'invert' | 'blur' | 'none', and the inert filtersProperty style prop is gone.

title: Chip never applies the group class, so its _group* recipe rules are dead
description: chip.ts sets _groupHover, _groupActive and _groupDisabled on the chipIcon slot, plus a .group hover rule for the selected state. All of them need an ancestor carrying the class 'group', which Chip.tsx never set. The library's idiom is to append ' group' to the interactive container's className, as Button, IconButton, FormField, DatePicker and TimePicker all do. Found while porting ecl.1.
close_reason: Chip.tsx appends ' group' to the body slot's className, matching the idiom in Button, IconButton and FormField. The body is the interactive element and the ancestor of chipIcon, so all five .group rules now match. Note this is a visual change: the chipIcon hover and active fills had never rendered.

title: Select: Create component (currently missing)
description:
## Current State
Select component directory may exist but no Select.tsx file found. This is a missing component.

## Architecture Decision
**Build as a wrapper around existing Menu functionality.** This leverages:
- Menu's floating-ui positioning
- Menu's keyboard navigation
- Menu's accessibility features
- Consistent behavior across components

## Implementation Approach
```tsx
// Select wraps Menu with select-specific semantics
<Select value={value} onChange={onChange} placeholder="Select...">
  <SelectOption value="1">Option 1</SelectOption>
  <SelectOption value="2">Option 2</SelectOption>
</Select>
```

## Component Parts (wrapping Menu equivalents)
- **Select** - Wraps Menu, manages selected value state
- **SelectTrigger** - Wraps MenuTrigger, displays selected value or placeholder
- **SelectOption** - Wraps MenuItem, adds selection indicator

## Key Differences from Menu
- Shows selected value in trigger (not just a button label)
- Single selection with value/onChange pattern
- Checkmark or highlight on selected option
- `role="listbox"` instead of `role="menu"`

## Features
- Keyboard navigation (inherited from Menu)
- Typeahead search (inherited from Menu)
- Disabled options
- Error state styling
- Placeholder text when no selection

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Wraps Menu component internally
- [ ] Single-select functionality works
- [ ] Selected value displays in trigger
- [ ] Keyboard accessible (inherited)
- [ ] Matches library visual style
- [ ] Disabled and error states
- [ ] Add Storybook story
close_reason: Completed - Select component implemented with full functionality

title: Card: Rebuild with interactive/non-interactive variants
description:
## Current State
Card always renders as button or anchor element. This is semantically incorrect for non-interactive cards (content containers).

## Current Problems
- Always interactive (`<button>` or `<a>`)
- No static/non-interactive variant
- `grabbed` prop suggests drag functionality that may not be implemented
- Missing semantic HTML options (`<article>`, `<section>`, `<div>`)

## Required Changes
1. **Default to non-interactive** - render as `<div>` or allow `as` prop
2. **Add `interactive` variant** - optionally renders as button/anchor
3. **Clean up props**:
   - Remove or properly implement `grabbed`
   - Add `as` prop support for semantic flexibility
   - Keep `href` for link cards
4. **Update recipe** with visual variants:
   - Default (non-interactive)
   - Interactive (hover/focus states)
   - Possibly: elevated, outlined, filled variants

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Non-interactive card renders as div by default
- [ ] Interactive prop enables button behavior
- [ ] href prop renders as anchor with proper accessibility
- [ ] Polymorphic `as` prop works (article, section, etc.)
- [ ] Visual variants implemented
- [ ] Add Storybook story showing all variants

title: Tooltip: Convert to floating-ui
description:
## Current State
Custom positioning implementation with ~200 lines of manual positioning logic, viewport detection, and clockwise fallback placement system.

## Required Changes
- Replace custom positioning with `@floating-ui/react`
- Use pattern established in Menu component:
  - `useFloating` hook with `flip()`, `shift()`, `offset()` middleware
  - `FloatingPortal` for proper stacking
  - `autoUpdate` for position tracking
- Add `useHover` and `useFocus` from floating-ui for trigger modes
- Simplify caret positioning using floating-ui's arrow middleware

## Benefits
- Consistent positioning behavior with Menu
- Better edge cases handled automatically
- Less code to maintain
- Accessibility improvements via floating-ui's role hooks

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tooltip renders correctly in all 12 positions
- [ ] Auto-flips when near viewport edges
- [ ] Caret points correctly
- [ ] Both hover and click triggers work
- [ ] Title + text content displays properly
- [ ] Add Storybook story demonstrating all variants

title: Breadcrumbs: Reassess and rebuild
description:
## Current State
Basic implementation using `<ul>` wrapped in Text component. Uses Link component for navigation items.

## Accessibility Issues
- Should use `<nav>` wrapper with aria-label="Breadcrumb"
- Should use `<ol>` (ordered list) not `<ul>` - breadcrumbs have order
- Current item should have aria-current="page"
- Separator (/) should be aria-hidden

## API Considerations
Current: `items: { id: string; label: string; href?: string }[]`
- Good that href is optional (current page won't have link)
- Consider adding icon support for items
- Consider max-items with collapse for long breadcrumbs

## Required Changes
1. Wrap in `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">`
2. Change to `<ol>` from `<ul>`
3. Add aria-current="page" to current item
4. Make separators aria-hidden
5. Review styling/recipe

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Proper semantic HTML (nav > ol > li)
- [ ] Correct ARIA attributes
- [ ] Links work correctly
- [ ] Current item styled differently (no link)
- [ ] Add Storybook story

2. **Shiki** - VS Code-quality highlighting, uses TextMate grammars

Recommendation: Start with Shiki for best quality, or Prism for smaller bundle.

## Component Structure
```tsx

}

```
